To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the LOH method is flawed in principle, that it is practically difficult to use, that it is not very useful for mapping tumor‐suppressor gene targets, and that it is unlikely to become a more effective technique.

the two‐hit model, as it is usually applied in LOH studies, is flawed, but that it can be salvaged by taking into account the problems of heterogeneity, normal cell contamination, karyotypically complex tumors, and homozygous deletion.
the two‐hit model of Knudson is conceptually flawed, practically flawed, and practically untestable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetics of the human papillomavirus (HPV) and the development of HPV vaccines.
the development and use of molecular genetic tools for the identification of tumor‐suppressor gene (TSG) loci.
the identification of the genetic basis of human disease, with particular emphasis on cancer and the development of new methods to achieve this aim.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LOH analysis is not a reliable method for identifying tumor‐suppressor loci.
the two‐hit model is not the only model that can explain the LOH data.
the Knudson “two hit” hypothesis is conceptually and practically flawed and that the LOH studies based on the two hit hypothesis have failed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been successful in the development of the first comprehensive, quantitative model of tumor development, which is based on the two‐hit theory of Knudson (1971).
we have not found the tumor suppressor gene in this region.
the two‐hit model is a good starting point, but that it is not sufficient to identify tumor‐ suppressor gene targets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two‐hit theory of Knudson is a useful heuristic but is not a good basis for the design of experiments to find tumor suppressor genes.
LOH analysis, although conceptually simple, is practically difficult.
loss of heterozygosis (LOH) analysis is not a reliable way to find tumor suppressor genes.
